<reason>A high-quality debate with strong framing on both sides: A's patchable-vs-structural distinction and "universality without monopoly" line were genuinely effective, and A's pressure questions were sharp. But B built more surviving routes to victory. B turned A's own exemplars into the motion's indictment ("universal financing in an employer costume," later "plural payers strapped to single-payer scaffolding"), showing A's model only guarantees access by state action that neutralizes the very tie the motion condemns. B's administrative-waste and bargaining-power case, raised from the opening, went unanswered across all of A's speeches — a clean, untouched efficiency route. B also neutralized A's strongest pressure question (the refused drug) with the letterhead symmetry point: Germany's pooled funds refuse the same drug, so A's celebrated exit changes nothing there; A never addressed this despite two later speeches. The firewall-versus-fuse funding clash ended roughly even. A's clipped Rebuttal 2 added a modest execution cost. Both sides were well-grounded with no fake precision, but B made the debate easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's A2 in Rebuttal 2: answering A's "remedy this year" challenge with an appeals channel plus the symmetry turn — in Germany every fund drawing on the same pool issues the same refusal, so "switching funds changes the letterhead on the rejection." It converted A's best pressure question into a wash and was never answered. Runner-up: B's opening-to-closing administrative-waste argument standing wholly unrebutted.</best_rebuttal>
